evidence_items.source_quote: Further evaluation with a non-contrast computed tomography (CT) head shows a ring-enhancing lesion in the left temporal region with perifocal edema, an eccentric, and an inflammatory granuloma (Figure 1).

rationale: A 24-year-old female presenting with recurrent tonic-clonic seizures and altered sensorium. Brain CT and MRI demonstrated ring-enhancing lesions in the left temporal and parietal lobes with perifocal edema, consistent with cysticercal encephalitis. Treated successfully with albendazole and anti-epileptic therapy.

evidence_items.source_quote: The MRI brain showed multiple small cysts with scolex in both the cerebral hemispheres and a giant intraparenchymal cyst measuring 5 x 4.3 cms in the right cerebral hemisphere [Figure 1a and b].

rationale: A 38-year-old female presenting with progressive pseudobulbar palsy and partial seizures. Brain MRI demonstrated pathognomonic multiple small cysts with visible scolex in both cerebral hemispheres and a giant intraparenchymal cyst. Serology was positive and symptoms responded to albendazole.

evidence_items.source_quote: Due to these findings, enzyme-linked immunoelectrotransfer blot (EITB) for anticysticercal antibodies was sent and was reportedly positive.

rationale: A 26-year-old female presenting with left oculomotor nerve palsy. Brain CT and MRI demonstrated midbrain and frontal ring-enhancing nodular calcified lesions consistent with NCC. Enzyme-linked immunoelectrotransfer blot (EITB) for anticysticercal antibodies was positive, and she recovered on albendazole and praziquantel.

evidence_items.source_quote: The cyst contains larval stage of parasite showing gut and scolex with muscular suckers and rostellum containing hooklets, suggestive of neurocysticercosis.
evidence_items.target_concept: Taenia solium larva with scolex, suckers, hooklets

rationale: A 24-year-old male presenting with acute obstructive hydrocephalus due to a third ventricular cyst. Surgical excision of the cyst was performed; histopathology confirmed the larval cestode with outer cuticle, suckers, and rostellum containing hooklets.

evidence_items.source_quote: Subsequent pathological findings showed fibrosis, local calcification, and chronic inflammation associated with the cysticercosis cyst walls.

rationale: A 64-year-old male presenting with acute hydrocephalus and lower extremity weakness. Thoraco-lumbar spine MRI demonstrated multiple contrast-enhancing intraspinal cysts extending C7 to S1. Surgical resection confirmed cysticercosis cyst walls on histopathology, and albendazole was administered.

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF cysticercus antibody ELISA testing was positive, and a diagnosis of racemose NCC was made based on the immunoassay results, neuroimaging findings, and a history of recent emigration from Mexico.

rationale: A 39-year-old male presenting with headaches and papilledema. Brain MRI demonstrated multiple nonenhancing cystic lesions in basal cisterns and ventricles characteristic of racemose NCC. CSF cysticercus antibody ELISA was positive, and prolonged albendazole therapy led to complete radiographic resolution.

evidence_items.source_quote: Neuropathology was consistent with neurocysticercosis in racemose cyst formation [Figure 5].

rationale: A 34-year-old male presenting with new-onset seizures and a fronto-temporal multilobulated cystic lesion. Serum cysticercosis IgG was positive, and surgical neuropathology confirmed racemose neurocysticercosis with microtriches and calcareous corpuscles.

evidence_items.source_quote: Noncontrast MRI of the neck showed a well-defined intramedullary cystic lesion at C4-C6 vertebral levels, which was hypointense on T1 weighted and hyperintense on T2 weighted images with peripheral, spinal cord edema having an intracystic hypointense on T2 weighted "target" like lesion suggestive of scolex.
evidence_items.target_concept: Taenia solium intramedullary cyst with scolex

rationale: A 6-year-old female presenting with neck stiffness. Cervical spine MRI revealed a well-defined intramedullary cystic lesion at C4-C6 with an intracystic hypointense target-like scolex, meeting absolute diagnostic criteria for neurocysticercosis. Serum Ag-ELISA was positive and she resolved completely on albendazole.

evidence_items.source_quote: we applied the revised diagnostic criteria for Taenia solium infection and discovered that our patient presented a definitive diagnosis of NCC due to the neuroimaging presence of cystic lesions without a discernible scolex and enhancing lesion plus previous household contact with T. solium and neurological clinical manifestations of NCC.
evidence_items.test_name: Del Brutto revised diagnostic criteria evaluation

rationale: A 64-year-old female post-allogeneic HSCT developing cerebellar cystic lesions with edema. Diagnosis of definitive neurocysticercosis was established based on Del Brutto revised criteria (suggestive multicystic lesions, household contact, clinical presentation, and documented resolution after albendazole).

evidence_items.source_quote: A Taenia solium-specific PCR targeting the pTsol9 repeat element based on a previous paper by Almeida and colleagues and a pan-Cestoda PCR targeting a fragment of the mitochondrial ribosomal RNA (16S rRNA - 12S rRNA) genes based on a paper by Le and colleagues were attempted.
evidence_items.test_name: Taenia solium-specific PCR on brain biopsy

rationale: A 35-year-old male presenting with first-onset seizure and a ring-enhancing temporal lobe lesion. Brain biopsy tissue subjected to PCR testing targeting the pTsol9 repeat element and sequencing confirmed Taenia solium DNA, with subsequent cure on albendazole.

evidence_items.source_quote: demonstrated a mature T. solium plerocercoid larvae measuring 1.2 x 0.5 x 0.2 cm encased in a tan, gelatinous, cystic membrane.
evidence_items.test_name: Pathological examination of resected ventricular mass
evidence_items.target_concept: Mature Taenia solium larva in fourth ventricle

rationale: A 36-year-old female presenting with headaches, vertigo, and hydrocephalus. Surgical resection of the fourth ventricular mass was performed; gross and pathological examination confirmed a mature Taenia solium larva encased in a cystic membrane.

evidence_items.source_quote: The classical imaging findings of multiple cysts with scolex on the MRI head are an absolute criterion for diagnosis of definitive NCC.
evidence_items.target_concept: Cysts with scolex on brain MRI

rationale: A 42-year-old male presenting following trauma. Contrast-enhanced brain MRI revealed multiple ring lesions with enhancing protoscolex representing pathognomonic neurocysticercosis, in conjunction with concomitant subretinal cysticerci. Treated with albendazole and dexamethasone.

evidence_items.source_quote: His cysticercosis antibody IgG serum (EIA) level was 2.05 (reference value <0.90).

rationale: A 31-year-old male presenting with headache and anxiety. Brain MRI revealed multiple T2-hyperintense parenchymal lesions across bilateral hemispheres and cerebellum with edema and calcification. Serum cysticercosis IgG antibody was positive (2.05), and symptoms resolved on albendazole and steroids.

evidence_items.source_quote: The histopathological report confirmed spinal NCC [Figure 3].

rationale: A 58-year-old female presenting with progressive paraplegia and sensory disturbance due to thoracic spinal cord compression. MRI showed multiple intradural extramedullary cysts at T4-T6 and T9-T11. Resection of cysts was performed and histopathology confirmed spinal neurocysticercosis; treated postoperatively with albendazole and corticosteroids.

evidence_items.source_quote: multiple cystic lesions, one with surrounding vasogenic edema in the left frontal lobe.
evidence_items.target_concept: Multiple cystic brain lesions with edema and calcification

rationale: A 24-year-old male immigrant from Central America presenting with recurrent tonic-clonic seizures. Brain CT and MRI demonstrated multiple cystic lesions with ring enhancement, surrounding vasogenic edema, and peripheral calcification, consistent with degenerative-phase neurocysticercosis. Successfully treated with albendazole and praziquantel.

evidence_items.source_quote: an intracerebral cyst of middle size (2.3 x 2.1 x 3 cm) was identified in the right frontal lobe [Figure 4].
evidence_items.target_concept: Intracerebral cystic lesion with calcified nodule and edema

rationale: A 22-year-old female presenting with generalized seizures and headaches. Head CT demonstrated a 2.3 x 2.1 x 3 cm intracerebral cyst in the right frontal lobe with a calcified nodule and surrounding brain edema, consistent with neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Just as soon as the endoscope passed through to the fourth ventricle, a cystic lesion was found, which was compatible with a neurocysti

rationale: A 51-year-old male presenting with acute intracranial hypertension and fourth ventricular dilatation. Rigid endoscopic exploration of the fourth ventricle revealed and completely excised a neurocysticercosis cyst, restoring CSF flow, followed by standard albendazole therapy.

evidence_items.source_quote: A ring lesion with an eccentric scolex in the fourth ventricle with no evidence of post-contrast enhancement was seen. Thus, an imaging diagnosis of isolated fourth ventricular NCC was made.
evidence_items.target_concept: Fourth ventricular cystic lesion with eccentric scolex

rationale: A 17-year-old male presenting with papilledema and hydrocephalus. Brain CISS-sequence MRI demonstrated a ring lesion with an eccentric scolex in the fourth ventricle with subsequent migration into the third and lateral ventricles; successfully treated with albendazole and endoscopic removal.

evidence_items.source_quote: Diagnostic cerebrospinal fluid analysis by nucleic acid amplification test was positive for anti-cysticercal antibodies; a final diagnosis of spinal neurocysticercosis was made.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF nucleic acid amplification test for anti-cysticercal antibodies

rationale: A 30-year-old male presenting with back pain and lower limb weakness. Spine MRI revealed an intramedullary ring-enhancing lesion with extensive cord edema at D11. CSF nucleic acid amplification test was positive for anti-cysticercal antibodies, confirming spinal neurocysticercosis; follow-up MRI showed marked reduction of lesion and cord edema on albendazole.

evidence_items.source_quote: Western blot assay detected specific antibodies against cysticercus (LDBIO DIAGNOSTICS, Lyon, France). Therefore the diagnosis of neurocysticercosis was made and the appropriated therapy was started
evidence_items.test_name: Western blot assay for cysticercus antibodies

rationale: A 6-year-old male immigrant presenting with prolonged focal motor seizures. Brain MRI showed two cystic lesions in the lentiform nucleus and frontoparietal lobe. Western blot assay detected specific anti-cysticercal antibodies; treated with albendazole and dexamethasone with complete lesion calcification and seizure freedom.

evidence_items.source_quote: NCC serology (ELISA for IgG antibodies) in serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) was positive with titers of 1:1600 and 1:80, respectively.
evidence_items.test_name: NCC IgG ELISA in serum and CSF

rationale: A 62-year-old female presenting with reversible dementia and gait disturbance. Brain MRI showed conglomerate cystic lesions in the sylvian fissure, basal cisterns, and 3rd ventricle characteristic of racemose NCC. NCC serology by ELISA was positive in both serum (1:1600) and CSF (1:80), with clinical recovery after shunting and steroids.

evidence_items.source_quote: Some of the lesions were showing eccentric nodules. No post-contrast enhancement was seen suggestive of the colloidal vesicular stage of neurocysticercosis.
evidence_items.target_concept: Taenia solium cystic lesions with eccentric scolex nodule

rationale: A 23-year-old female presenting with mania and seizures. Brain MRI demonstrated multiple T2-hyperintense parenchymal cystic lesions in both cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres, some showing eccentric nodules pathognomonic for vesicular neurocysticercosis; responded to albendazole and steroids.

evidence_items.source_quote: The pathology report confirmed the cyst to be a T. solium larva in its vesicular stage as had already been suspected [Figure 4].

rationale: A 36-year-old female presenting with headaches, papilledema, and hydrocephalus caused by a mobile 4th ventricle cyst. Microsurgical resection was performed; histopathology confirmed a Taenia solium larva in its vesicular stage.

evidence_items.source_quote: There were multiple cysts in the right Sylvian fissure, without scolex, and peripheral enhancement, whose appearance resembled a "bunch of grapes" (Figure 2, A, B and C).

rationale: A 63-year-old woman evaluated for gait disorder, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence with a long-standing history of neurocysticercosis. Brain MRI revealed multiple cysts in the Sylvian fissure resembling a bunch of grapes characteristic of racemose neurocysticercosis, which improved with shunt placement and anti-parasitic/corticosteroid therapy.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histological examination revealed a parasitic wall characterized by wavy, dense cuticle, and focal globular structure, surrounding inflammatory, mononuclear lymphocytic reaction with plasma cells [Figure 3]. Postoperative lentil lectin glycoprotein enzyme-linked immunoelectrotransfer blot was positive. These findings were compatible with cysticercosis cyst.

rationale: A 45-year-old woman presenting with severe headaches and bitemporal hemianopia due to a sellar/suprasellar cyst. Resection biopsy revealed parasitic cuticle with mononuclear reaction, and postoperative LLGP-EITB was positive, confirming neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: The preliminary pathological report returned as neurocysticercosis (shown in Figure 3).

rationale: A 37-year-old woman presenting with progressive bilateral lower extremity weakness found to have a ring-enhancing intramedullary spinal cord lesion at T8. Resection and pathology confirmed neurocysticercosis, and she improved following albendazole and dexamethasone therapy.

evidence_items.source_quote: A computed tomographic scan of the brain and chest revealed multiple nodular and small calcified densities (Fig. 3, 4).

rationale: A 65-year-old man presenting with generalized weakness, subcutaneous nodules, and pulmonary densities. Brain and chest CT revealed multiple nodular and small calcified densities, and biopsies of subcutaneous and pulmonary nodules confirmed cysticercosis, establishing disseminated cysticercosis with neurocysticercosis comorbidity.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histological analysis confirmed NCC.

rationale: A 39-year-old woman presenting with severe headaches and gait ataxia due to a fourth ventricle cyst with an enhancing scolex causing obstructive hydrocephalus. Surgical resection and histological analysis confirmed neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Meanwhile the diagnosis of NC was confirmed by serological tests detecting Taenia solium antigen and antibodies (ELISA) in the CSF and serum.

rationale: A 29-year-old woman presenting with acute hydrocephalus due to a free-floating intraventricular cyst and occipital parenchymal calcification. Diagnosis was confirmed by serological tests detecting Taenia solium antigen and antibodies in CSF and serum.

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF examination done revealed elevated protein and normal glucose levels with increased lymphocytes, and few eosinophils and positive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for anti-T. solium IgG immunoglobulin.

rationale: A 10-year-old female presenting with spastic paraplegia due to an intramedullary thoracic spinal cord cystic lesion at D3-D4. CSF ELISA was positive for anti-T. solium IgG, and she made a complete recovery following antihelminthic and corticosteroid therapy.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathology showed typical larvae of Taenia solium, collagenous cyst wall without surrounding reactive changes.

rationale: Patient treated surgically for an intracranial cyst with histopathology demonstrating typical larvae of Taenia solium and collagenous cyst wall, followed by successful albendazole therapy with no recurrence on 2-year follow-up MRI.

evidence_items.source_quote: Examination of the brain showed obstructive hydrocephalus, bilateral uncal herniation, flattening of the cerebral gyri, and an intact cysticercus compressing the inferior 4th ventricle (Figure 1).

rationale: A teenage girl presenting with severe headaches initially misdiagnosed as tension headaches who died from uncal herniation. Autopsy revealed obstructive hydrocephalus and an intact cysticercus compressing the inferior fourth ventricle, confirming fatal intraventricular neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Based on the obtained histopathological results, we were able to confirm our preliminary diagnosis of neurocysticercosis, to start the patient on high-dose dexamethasone followed by albendazole to eliminate any still-unidentifiable minute cysticerci.

rationale: A 42-year-old man presenting with acute hydrocephalus from an obstructive right lateral ventricle cyst with eccentric mural nodule. CSF ELISA demonstrated cysticercus antibodies, and endoscopic extraction confirmed a scolex on histopathology, establishing confirmed neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Their histopathology proved to be a whole cysticercus (Figure 3(a)) and a broken aneurysm with a coagulum in formation (Figure 3(b)).

rationale: A 49-year-old woman presenting with subarachnoid hemorrhage from a middle cerebral artery aneurysm. During surgical clipping, a 2-cm cyst was excised, and histopathology confirmed a whole cysticercus; postoperative CT showed multiple brain calcifications and Sylvian cysts, treated with albendazole.

evidence_items.source_quote: A diagnosis of third ventricular cysticercosis causing obstructive hydrocephalus was made.

rationale: A 42-year-old male presenting with seizures and headaches due to a third ventricular cystic lesion with an eccentric mural nodule (scolex) causing hydrocephalus. Follow-up imaging demonstrated cyst migration into the occipital horn of the lateral ventricle, and albendazole therapy led to complete resolution.

evidence_items.source_quote: MRI brain of the patient showed a typical well-defined cystic lesion with intracavitary scolex on the right side of mid pons [Figure 3]. The evidence of a typical scolex on a CT or MRI is considered the absolute criteria for diagnosis of neurocysticercosis.

rationale: A 35-year-old man presenting with acute headache, giddiness, and WEMINO syndrome. Brain MRI demonstrated an absolute Del Brutto criterion of a cystic lesion with intracavitary scolex in the mid pons, resolving completely with albendazole and steroids.

evidence_items.source_quote: A Brain CT scan was ordered which revealed multiple calcified and vesicular cysts within the Brain parenchyma; features consistent with Neurocysticercosis.
evidence_items.target_concept: Multiple vesicular and calcified brain cysts

rationale: A 13-year-old girl presenting with drug-resistant epilepsy. Brain CT scan revealed multiple calcified and vesicular cysts in the brain parenchyma consistent with neurocysticercosis, which showed marked reduction in active cysts following one month of albendazole.

evidence_items.source_quote: The histological picture was suggestive of a necrotic parasite, unclassified.

rationale: A 9-year-old girl presenting with focal partial seizures and a ring-enhancing frontal lobe lesion with surrounding edema. She responded to albendazole with reduction of edema, and stereotactic surgical resection confirmed a calcified necrotic parasite compatible with a degenerated solitary cysticercus granuloma.

evidence_items.source_quote: Due to the clinical deterioration of the patient and the lack of a clear diagnosis, a biopsy of the cyst was performed with evidence of a cysticercus cyst (Figure 3).

rationale: A 51-year-old male presenting with gait instability, cognitive decline, and a cerebellar cyst on CT/MRI. Surgical biopsy demonstrated a cysticercus cyst, and he was diagnosed with racemose neurocysticercosis with cerebellar involvement and treated with albendazole and dexamethasone.

evidence_items.source_quote: The CT brain indicated hypodense regions in the right frontal and parietal lobes, as well as abnormal and irregular calcifications (Figure 1).

rationale: A 37-year-old female presenting with acute psychosis and hallucinations with a documented collateral history of seizures and prior untreated neurocysticercosis. CT and MRI brain demonstrated characteristic irregular calcifications and encephalomalacia, confirming neurocysticercosis as a contributory comorbidity to secondary psychosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathology report showed findings compatible with cysticercosis [Figure 3].

rationale: A 28-year-old male presenting with vision loss and temporal hemianopia due to a suprasellar cystic lesion. Surgical pterional craniotomy visualized the scolex in the cyst, and histopathology confirmed cysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Through this admission, he developed a seizure with suggestive MRI of neurocysticercosis and received Albendazole with steroids.

rationale: A 30-year-old male admitted with refractory TTP who developed acute seizures during hospitalization with brain MRI findings suggestive of neurocysticercosis, treated successfully with albendazole and corticosteroids.

evidence_items.source_quote: She was diagnosed with vesicular stage of parenchymal neurocysticercosis.

rationale: A 4-year-old child presenting with seizures diagnosed with vesicular stage parenchymal neurocysticercosis on neuroimaging, treated successfully with albendazole and prednisolone.

evidence_items.source_quote: A diagnosis of vesicular and calcified stages of parenchymal neurocysticercosis was made.

rationale: A 7-year-old child presenting with focal seizures diagnosed with vesicular and calcified stages of parenchymal neurocysticercosis on neuroimaging, with ocular cysticercosis ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: Those suggested a massive neurocysticercosis lesions with intra parenchymatous vesicular cysts in supra and sub-tentorial and meningeal localization including racemose forms with communicating hydrocephalus.

rationale: A 42-year-old male presenting with chronic headaches, seizures, and hydrocephalus with CT and MRI demonstrating massive intraparenchymal vesicular cysts and meningeal racemose neurocysticercosis meeting Del Brutto absolute criteria.

evidence_items.source_quote: Based on the histopathological results, the patients were diagnosed with intraventricular neurocysticercosis and prescribed cysticidal drugs such as albendazole for 30 days.

rationale: Two patients presenting with hydrocephalus and ventricular masses on MRI. Microsurgical resection yielded specimens containing larvae and mummified dead larvae confirming intraventricular neurocysticercosis on histopathology, treated with albendazole.

evidence_items.source_quote: Based on imaging findings, a diagnosis of racemose NCC was made.

rationale: A 45-year-old female presenting with headaches and seizures found to have a multiloculated cystic lesion in the basal cisterns on brain MRI. Based on typical neuroimaging findings without scolex, a diagnosis of racemose neurocysticercosis was made.

evidence_items.source_quote: MRI brain revealed a multiloculated cystic lesion in the pineal region extending into the third ventricle with resultant obstruction (Figure 2).

rationale: A 10-year-old boy presenting with headaches, seizures, and visual disturbances due to a multiloculated cystic lesion in the pineal region extending into the third ventricle showing the classic cluster of grapes appearance pathognomonic for racemose neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: MRI revealed dilatation of the extra-axial CSF spaces with septations along the inferior aspect of the corpus callosum.

rationale: A 37-year-old male presenting with frequent headaches and recurrent seizures. Brain MRI and FIESTA revealed multiseptated cystic dilatation of the extra-axial CSF spaces and basal cisterns characteristic of racemose neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: On FIESTA MRI (Figure 4C and D), the lesion showed thin septations in the ambient cistern and Sylvian fissures, which strongly suggested the diagnosis of racemose NCC.

rationale: A 56-year-old male presenting with seizures, ataxia, and dementia who failed empiric tuberculosis treatment. FIESTA MRI demonstrated thin septations in the dilated ambient cistern and Sylvian fissures strongly confirming racemose neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Multiple calcifications typical for neurocysticercosis were seen in the cerebral parenchyma, basal ganglia, and cerebellum (Figures 1-3).

rationale: A 47-year-old male living with HIV found on screening to have extensive calcified neurocysticercosis. Multiple calcifications typical for neurocysticercosis were seen across cerebral parenchyma and cerebellum, with positive LDBIO cysticercosis IgG Western Blot.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cranial magnetic resonance imaging was performed and showed findings consistent with active-phase NCC (Figure 2).

rationale: A patient presenting with neurological manifestations found to have active-phase neurocysticercosis on cranial MRI concordant with positive Taenia solium serology, establishing confirmed neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Despite negative serology, a diagnosis of NCC was made based on the patient's clinical presentation, his history of immigration from an endemic region, and neuroimaging findings consistent with cystic lesions, as outlined in the Del Brutto diagnostic criteria.

rationale: A 49-year-old male immigrant from Guatemala presenting with seizures and multiple intracranial calcified and cystic lesions on CT and MRI. Despite negative serology, the diagnosis of neurocysticercosis was confirmed based on Del Brutto diagnostic criteria and clinical improvement on albendazole and levetiracetam.

step4_condition_matched: Calcified parenchymal neurocysticercosis with perilesional edema

evidence_items.source_quote: As part of the routine workup for altered mental status, a CT Brain (Figure 1) was performed on September 14, 2025, showing a 3 mm cortical calcification with perilesional edema in the inferior posterior left frontal lobe, consistent with calcified parenchymal neurocysticercosis.

rationale: A 28-year-old male presenting with altered mental status and behavioral changes. Brain CT revealed a 3 mm cortical calcification with perilesional edema in the left frontal lobe consistent with calcified parenchymal neurocysticercosis, confirmed on follow-up MRI showing a solitary ring-enhancing lesion with central calcification.
